newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy bourse fails to open due technical problems.
newsitem.headline: Italy bourse fails to open due technical problems.

text.p: Italy's stock exchange failed to open Monday as the Milan bourse experienced serious technical problems for the first time since it started moving towards screen-based trading in 1991.

A spokesman for the bourse council said that the stock market had suffered from a serious breakdown of its hardware and software systems Monday morning. This came after a number of temporary breakdowns in trading throughout last week.
Dealers said that this was just another setback for the reputation of the Milan bourse and its attempts to take its place alongside the major European stock markets of London, Paris and Frankfurt.

International investors are already wary of investing in Italian stocks due to worries that market regulations are not tight enough, as a number of large Italian listed companies have hit major financial problems with shareholders often surprised to see the severity of the crisis.

Dealers said that investors have suffered as groups such as Ferruzzi Finanziaria (now renamed Compart) Montedison, Gemina, Banco di Napoli and most recently Olivetti have shocked their shareholders on the size of their financial problems.
